title: Occupationally Exposed and General Population Antibody Profiles to Influenza A Viruses Circulating in Swine as Indication of Zoonotic Risk.
abstract: Persons with occupational exposure to swine might be at disproportionate risk for zoonotic swine influenza A virus. To evaluate human antibody responses, we tested serum or plasma from swine veterinarian, farm employee, and general population cohorts by hemagglutination inhibition assays against representative swine and human seasonal influenza vaccine strains. We analyzed hemagglutination inhibition data by antigenic cartography to assess strain relationships and reproduction number modeling to evaluate pandemic potential using age-stratified immunity profiles. Occupationally exposed groups had lower human seasonal vaccine uptake (45.5% vs. 70%) and lower odds of seropositivity to several H1 and H3 strains from swine than did general population cohorts. One swine strain exhibited significant antigenic drift (3.62 antigenic units) from its nearest vaccine strain. Multiple strains required lower reproduction number thresholds for pandemic spread (1.09-1.35) than recorded pandemic strains (1.46-1.80), demonstrating that population immunity gaps heighten zoonotic risk to circulating swine H1 and H3 strains.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated antibody profiles to swine influenza A viruses in occupationally exposed and general populations. Swine veterinarians and farm employees showed lower vaccine uptake and seropositivity to swine H1 and H3 strains compared to the general population. title: First report of human infection caused by swine-origin influenza A(H1N2)v virus in mainland China: a confirmed case identified through influenza-like illness surveillance, Kunming (Yunnan), 2025
abstract: Objective This case report details the epidemiological characteristics of the first human case of swine-origin influenza A(H1N2)v infection identified in mainland China, to formulate guidelines for the prevention and control of human swine-origin influenza A (H1N2) virus infections. Methods Clinical and epidemiological data of the case were collected through field epidemiological investigation combined with laboratory testing. Specimens were collected from the patient, close contacts, animals subjects (including one deceased pig), and environmental matrices and analyzed to trace the potential infection source and characterize the clinical and epidemiological features. Results This study describes a sporadic, isolated case of human infection with swine influenza A(H1N2)v in mainland China, with no evidence of human-to-human transmission. Prior to symptom onset, the patient inhabited a high-risk mixed residential setting with frequent close exposure to domestic livestock and poultry. Specially, his townhouse stood adjacent to his great-uncle’s residence, where swine were raised; the great-uncle also documented the mortality of one pig. But had no contact with human confirmed cases presenting similar clinical manifestations. Testing of the collected specimens confirmed influenza N2 subtype positivity in lung tissue specimens obtained from the deceased pigs, whereas all remaining animal and environmental specimens yielded negative test results. elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是 2025 年在昆明(云南)利用现场 流行病学 和对患者、接触者、动物和环境标本进行实验室检测进行的单一人类病例调查。

abstract_zh: 目的 详细介绍中国大陆首例人源甲型H1N2流感病毒感染病例的流行病学特征,为制定人源性甲型H1N2流感病毒感染防控指南提供依据。方法通过现场流行病学调查结合实验室检测,收集该病例的临床和流行病学资料。从患者、密切接触者、动物受试者(包括一头死猪)和环境基质中收集样本并进行分析,以追踪潜在的感染源并描述临床和流行病学特征。结果本研究描述了中国大陆发生的一例散发性、孤立的人感染甲型H1N2猪流感病例,没有人传人传播的证据。症状出现前,患者居住在高风险混合住宅环境中,经常近距离接触家畜和家禽。特别是,他的联排别墅毗邻他叔公的住所,那里养猪;叔公还记录了一只猪的死亡率。但没有接触过出现类似临床表现的人类确诊病例。对收集的样本进行检测证实,从死猪身上获得的肺组织样本中呈流感 N2 亚型阳性,而所有剩余的动物和环境样本的检测结果均为阴性。患者最终在临床康复后出院。共有30名密切接触者完成自我健康监测和咽拭子筛查。在整个监测期间,这些人没有出现流感样疾病,所有咽拭子样本检测结果均为阴性。医学监测未发现继发病例,并相应实施了有针对性的环境消毒。结论 初步判断该病例的可能传染源为携带N2亚型甲型流感病毒的死猪。因此,A(H1N2)v等新型流感亚型的增强型监测和改良型猪流感疫苗接种对于有针对性地预防和控制这些新兴病毒引起的人类感染至关重要。

title: SNHG15 Positively Regulates Influenza Virus Infection Through Its Association With miR-153 and RABL2A.
abstract: Influenza viruses cause seasonal epidemics, and current vaccines do not fully protect against them. This study focuses on long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), which are RNA molecules that do not code for proteins but play crucial roles in various biological processes. We identified 17 lncRNAs altered by the influenza virus. Among these, SNHG15 was found to enhance influenza virus infection. Knockdown of SNHG15 using CRISPR interference and RNA interference reduced influenza virus infection, while overexpression of SNHG15 increased virus replication. We found that miR-153-3p, a competitive endogenous RNA (ceRNA) for SNHG15, acts as an anti-influenza microRNA, and its overexpression negated SNHG15's proviral activity. RNA pull-down and mass spectrometry identified Rab-like protein 2A (RABL2A) as an interacting partner of SNHG15. Both SNHG15 and RABL2A facilitated influenza virus internalization. Additionally, siRNA-mediated knockdown of RABL2A reduced SNHG15-mediated virus internalization. In conclusion, SNHG15 enhances influenza A virus infection through its interactions with miR-153 and RABL2A.

title: Vaccine Literacy, Knowledge, and Acceptance Among University Students in the West Bank, Palestine: A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study of Health and Non-Health Students
abstract: Abstract Background Vaccine hesitancy remains a significant public health challenge globally, and vaccine literacy is increasingly recognized as a key determinant of vaccine acceptance. Data on vaccine literacy and acceptance among university students in Palestine are scarce, and no study has directly compared these outcomes across health and non-health disciplines in this setting. This study aimed to assess vaccine literacy, knowledge, and acceptance among Palestinian university students and identify associated factors with vaccine acceptance. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted at multiple universities across the West Bank, Palestine, during the 2025–2026 academic year. A total of 633 university students completed a structured, self-administered questionnaire distributed via Google Forms. The instrument comprised four sections assessing sociodemographic characteristics, vaccination history and information sources, vaccine knowledge (10 binary items), and vaccine literacy and acceptance using validated five-point Likert scales. title: Social influence versus fear in COVID-19 vaccine acceptance: insights for health marketing communication
abstract: Purpose This paper examines how fear (of COVID-19 and of COVID-19 vaccine side effects) and social influence jointly and individually affect the intention to receive the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine. This study aims to fill a gap in health and pharmaceutical marketing research by clarifying the relative importance of emotional versus social drivers of vaccine acceptance. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative survey of 600 adults residing in Spain was conducted using quota sampling for age and gender (gender quotas were partially unmet). Respondents evaluated fear of COVID-19, fear of vaccine side effects, social influence and intention to vaccinate using established scales. Consistent partial least squares structural equation modelling was used to assess measurement validity and to compare three models: a joint model including all predictors, a fear-only model and a social-influence-only model. Findings Fear of COVID-19 has a positive effect on vaccination intention, while fear of vaccine side effects has a negative effect. Social influence shows a strong positive effect and is the most influential predictor across all models. When considered jointly, social influence substantially reduces the explanatory power of fear, indicating that trusted individuals and institutions shape vaccination decisions more decisively than emotional responses. Research limitations/implications Results are limited to Spain and to the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine during a specific time period. Replication in other countries, vaccine types and socio-economic contexts is recommended. Nevertheless, the findings may be particularly relevant for contexts similar to that generated by the COVID-19 pandemic, in which both the disease and the potential effects of the vaccine were largely unknown, resulting in levels of uncertainty substantially higher than those associated with well-established diseases and vaccines, such as seasonal influenza. Practical implications Health communication and pharmaceutical marketing strategies should prioritize credible institutional messaging and trusted influencers rather than fear-based appeals. Addressing misinformation and strengthening institutional trust are essential. Originality/value This study offers an original analytical focus by providing the first comparative analysis of joint versus individual effects of fear and social influence on COVID-19 vaccination intention, offering new insights for health marketing strategy design.
journal: International Journal of Pharmaceutical and Healthcare Marketing

Design/methodology/approach A quantitative survey of 600 adults residing in Spain was conducted using quota sampling for age and gender (gender quotas were partially unmet). Respondents evaluated fear of COVID-19, fear of vaccine side effects, social influence and intention to vaccinate using established scales. Consistent partial least squares structural equation modelling was used to assess measurement validity and to compare three models: a joint model including all predictors, a fear-only model and a social-influence-only model. Findings Fear of COVID-19 has a positive effect on vaccination intention, while fear of vaccine side effects has a negative effect. Social influence shows a strong positive effect and is the most influential predictor across all models. When considered jointly, social influence substantially reduces the explanatory power of fear, indicating that trusted individuals and institutions shape vaccination decisions more decisively than emotional responses. Research limitations/implications Results are limited to Spain and to the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine during a specific time period. Replication in other countries, vaccine types and socio-economic contexts is recommended. Nevertheless, the findings may be particularly relevant for contexts similar to that generated by the COVID-19 pandemic, in which both the disease and the potential effects of the vaccine were largely unknown, resulting in levels of uncertainty substantially higher than those associated with well-established diseases and vaccines, such as seasonal influenza. Practical implications Health communication and pharmaceutical marketing strategies should prioritize credible institutional messaging and trusted influencers rather than fear-based appeals. Addressing misinformation and strengthening institutional trust are essential. Originality/value This study offers an original analytical focus by providing the first comparative analysis of joint versus individual effects of fear and social influence on COVID-19 vaccination intention, offering new insights for health marketing strategy design.

abstract_zh: 目的 本文研究了恐惧(对 COVID-19 和 COVID-19 疫苗 副作用)和社会影响如何共同和单独影响接受牛津-阿斯利康 疫苗 的意图。本研究旨在通过阐明 疫苗 接受度的情感驱动因素与社会驱动因素的相对重要性,来填补健康和药品营销研究的空白。设计/方法/途径 对居住在西班牙的 600 名成年人进行了定量调查,采用年龄和性别配额抽样(性别配额部分未满足)。受访者使用既定量表评估了对 COVID-19 的恐惧、对 疫苗 副作用的恐惧、社会影响和接种疫苗的意愿。使用一致的偏最小二乘结构方程模型来评估测量有效性并比较三个模型:包括所有预测变量的联合模型、仅恐惧模型和仅社会影响模型。研究结果对 COVID-19 的恐惧对 疫苗接种 意图有积极影响,而对 疫苗 副作用的恐惧则有负面影响。社会影响力显示出强烈的积极影响,并且是所有模型中最具影响力的预测因子。综合考虑时,社会影响力大大降低了恐惧的解释力,这表明受信任的个人和机构比情绪反应更能决定性地制定 疫苗接种 决策。研究限制/影响 结果仅限于特定时间段内的西班牙和牛津-阿斯利康 疫苗。建议在其他国家、疫苗 类型和社会经济环境中进行复制。然而,这些发现可能与类似于 COVID-19 大流行所产生的情况特别相关,在这种情况下,疾病和 疫苗 的潜在影响在很大程度上都是未知的,导致不确定性水平大大高于与既定疾病和 疫苗(例如 季节性流感)相关的不确定性水平。实际影响 健康传播和药品营销策略应优先考虑可信的机构信息和值得信赖的影响者,而不是基于恐惧的诉求。解决错误信息和加强机构信任至关重要。原创性/价值本研究首次对恐惧和社会影响对 COVID-19 疫苗接种 意图的联合与个体影响进行比较分析,提供了原创性的分析重点,为健康营销策略设计提供了新的见解。

title: FluEvoFormer: A Structure-Guided Generative Foundation Model for Prospective Influenza Antigenic Evolution and Vaccine Strain Selection
abstract: Seasonal influenza vaccine strain selection remains challenging because circulating viruses may drift after vaccine recommendations are made. This study presents FluEvoFormer, a structure-guided generative foundation model for prospective influenza antigenic evolution forecasting and vaccine strain ranking. The framework jointly encodes hemagglutinin and neuraminidase sequences and incorporates residue-contact graphs. Separate prediction heads estimate future viral dominance and the vaccine–virus antigenic match. Controlled future-like variant stress testing, uncertainty adjustments, and clade balancing are then used to rank vaccine candidates. A rolling retrospective evaluation was performed for target seasons involving the influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus and influenza A(H3N2) virus. The evaluation used cutoff-restricted sequence records, hemagglutination inhibition data, vaccine-composition records, protein-structure resources, and vaccine-effectiveness indicators. The historical training corpus for the influenza A(H1N1) virus also contained pre-2009 seasonal records. FluEvoFormer achieved the lowest held-out antigenicity prediction error, with mean absolute error (MAE) values of 0.389 for the combined historical influenza A(H1N1) virus corpus and 0.456 for the influenza A(H3N2) virus corpus. It also improved the future dominance prediction, with Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence values of 0.255 and 0.289, respectively. The model selected candidates with higher empirical normalized coverage scores in seven out of 10 influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 virus seasons and nine out of 10 influenza A(H3N2) virus seasons. The predicted coverage score showed a strong positive correlation with external vaccine-effectiveness estimates. These findings support FluEvoFormer as a computational decision-support framework for prioritizing influenza vaccine candidates before downstream laboratory and public health evaluations.

title: Multivariate influenza forecasting using time-series foundation models: a comparative study with classical statistical models using 11 years of surveillance data in Hong Kong
abstract: Accurate short-term forecasts of influenza activity are critical for public health preparedness but remain challenging with classical statistical models that depend on long historical data and often fail under data scarcity. Time-series foundation models (TSFMs), pretrained on large heterogeneous datasets, may offer improved accuracy and data efficiency through transferable temporal representations. We analyzed 605 weeks of influenza surveillance data from Hong Kong (2014–2025), including consultation rates, laboratory detections, hospital admissions, severe cases, and school outbreaks. Six TSFMs (Google TimesFM, Amazon Chronos, IBM Granite Tiny Time Mixers [TTM], Timer-XL, Moirai-MoE, and UniTS) were compared with OLS, GLM, SARIMA, and empirical Bayesian models in a rolling-origin design generating one- to four-week forecasts. Forecast accuracy was evaluated using R 2 , RMSE, symmetric MAPE, weighted interval score (WIS) and multivariable residual diagnostics. We further estimated the minimal input window required for R 2 ≥ 0.50 and the maximum credible forecast horizon (R 2 ≥ 0.50 with significant RMSE gain vs. Chronos, TimesFM, and SARIMA achieved the best overall one-week performance (R 2 0.88–0.89; RMSE 30.6–31.3), significantly outperforming OLS (R 2 0.78; p < 0.0001) and GLM (R 2 0.79; p < 0.0001). Chronos outperformed other models in two-to-four-week performance. Chronos produced credible forecasts of the multivariate influenza surveillance predictions up to three weeks (R 2 ≥ 0.50; p < 0.05), whereas classical models fell below threshold beyond two weeks. TSFMs required as low as eight weeks of input data to achieve R 2 ≥ 0.50, compared to at least 297 weeks for classical models. TSFMs deliver comparatively more accurate, well-calibrated, and data-efficient epidemic forecasts, capturing temporal and inter-variable dependencies than classical regression models. Their ability to generate more reliable forecasts from minimal historical data compared to classical approaches supports their potential for rapid deployment in seasonal influenza surveillance and emerging pandemics such as COVID-19.

title: Maternal influenza vaccination boosts durable breast milk antibody-mediated protection in infants
abstract: Influenza contributes to significant disease burden worldwide, and young infants are at an increased risk of severe influenza infection. Maternal antibodies transferred across the placenta and through breast milk confer anti-influenza immunity to the newborn. Placental transfer provides a finite window of protection, but breast milk antibody transfer may provide prolonged immunity across the postnatal period. Yet, how breastmilk antibody profiles are shaped by maternal vaccination, change postnatally, and whether they contribute to protection against influenza remains incompletely defined. Comprehensive systems serological analysis of influenza-specific antibodies across 21 different antigens in a longitudinal birth cohort revealed maternal influenza vaccination was associated with enhanced antibody-dependent complement deposition (ADCD) and FcγR binding in breast milk at two weeks postpartum. This effect was further stratified by trimester of vaccination: first trimester vaccinees exhibited increased ADCD and IgM levels, whereas second or third trimester vaccination was associated with increased FcγR and FcαR binding. Analysis of longitudinal samples revealed that anti-influenza antibody responses in milk shift postpartum toward increased FcγR binding and decreased ADCD activity and IgM levels. Finally, baseline ADCD activity in breast milk and serum IgG1 levels were identified as signatures of resistance to influenza infection during the first six months of life. A multivariate model combining correlates of protection across milk and serum compartments offered greater predictive power compared to either compartment alone, suggesting both routes of antibody transfer bolster anti-influenza immunity in infants. These data collectively suggest that maternal influenza vaccination confers infant protection via breast milk to augment placental antibody transfer, and the functional capacity of these protective antibodies could be enhanced with prolonged breastfeeding.

Maternal antibodies transferred across the placenta and through breast milk confer anti-influenza immunity to the newborn.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved a longitudinal birth cohort to analyze influenza-specific antibodies across 21 different antigens in breast milk and serum compartments.
analysis.methods: Comprehensive systems serological analysis was performed to assess antibody-dependent complement deposition (ADCD), FcγR binding, FcαR binding, and IgM levels in breast milk and serum samples.
analysis.main_results: Maternal influenza vaccination was associated with enhanced ADCD and FcγR binding in breast milk at two weeks postpartum, with effects stratified by trimester of vaccination. Longitudinal analysis revealed postpartum shifts toward increased FcγR binding and decreased ADCD activity and IgM levels.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that maternal influenza vaccination confers infant protection via breast milk to augment placental antibody transfer, and the functional capacity of these protective antibodies could be enhanced with prolonged breastfeeding.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that maternal vaccination and breastfeeding strategies could be optimized to enhance infant protection against influenza, with baseline ADCD activity in breast milk and serum IgG1 levels identified as signatures of resistance to infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to observational data from a single birth cohort, but the comprehensive systems serological approach and longitudinal design provide moderate evidence for the protective role of breast milk antibodies.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated how maternal influenza vaccination shapes breast milk antibody profiles and their contribution to infant protection. Using a longitudinal birth cohort, the researchers found that maternal vaccination enhanced functional antibody activities in breast milk, with effects varying by trimester of vaccination. Longitudinal analysis revealed postpartum shifts in antibody functions, and baseline ADCD activity and serum IgG1 levels were identified as protective signatures. The multivariate model combining milk and serum compartments showed greater predictive power, suggesting both antibody transfer routes bolster infant immunity. These findings support the importance of maternal vaccination and prolonged breastfeeding for infant influenza protection.

title_zh: 母体流感 疫苗接种 增强婴儿母乳抗体介导的持久保护
source_body_en: Influenza contributes to significant disease burden worldwide, and young infants are at an increased risk of severe influenza infection. Maternal antibodies transferred across the placenta and through breast milk confer anti-influenza immunity to the newborn. Placental transfer provides a finite window of protection, but breast milk antibody transfer may provide prolonged immunity across the postnatal period. Yet, how breastmilk antibody profiles are shaped by maternal vaccination, change postnatally, and whether they contribute to protection against influenza remains incompletely defined. Comprehensive systems serological analysis of influenza-specific antibodies across 21 different antigens in a longitudinal birth cohort revealed maternal influenza vaccination was associated with enhanced antibody-dependent complement deposition (ADCD) and FcγR binding in breast milk at two weeks postpartum. This effect was further stratified by trimester of vaccination: first trimester vaccinees exhibited increased ADCD and IgM levels, whereas second or third trimester vaccination was associated with increased FcγR and FcαR binding. Analysis of longitudinal samples revealed that anti-influenza antibody responses in milk shift postpartum toward increased FcγR binding and decreased ADCD activity and IgM levels. Finally, baseline ADCD activity in breast milk and serum IgG1 levels were identified as signatures of resistance to influenza infection during the first six months of life. A multivariate model combining correlates of protection across milk and serum compartments offered greater predictive power compared to either compartment alone, suggesting both routes of antibody transfer bolster anti-influenza immunity in infants. These data collectively suggest that maternal influenza vaccination confers infant protection via breast milk to augment placental antibody transfer, and the functional capacity of these protective antibodies could be enhanced with prolonged breastfeeding.
abstract_zh: 流感给全世界带来了巨大的疾病负担,小婴儿感染严重流感的风险增加。通过胎盘和母乳转移的母体抗体赋予新生儿抗流感免疫力。胎盘移植提供了有限的保护窗口,但母乳抗体移植可以在整个产后期间提供长期的免疫力。然而,母乳抗体谱如何由母体 疫苗接种 形成、在出生后发生变化以及它们是否有助于预防流感仍不完全明确。对纵向出生 队列研究 中 21 种不同抗原的流感特异性抗体的综合系统血清学分析显示,母体流感 疫苗接种 与产后两周母乳中抗体依赖性补体沉积 (ADCD) 和 FcγR 结合增强相关。这种效应通过 疫苗接种 的妊娠期进一步分层:妊娠早期 疫苗 表现出 ADCD 和 IgM 水平增加,而妊娠中期或晚期 疫苗接种 与 FcγR 和 FcαR 结合增加相关。纵向样本分析表明,产后乳汁中的抗流感抗体反应转向增加 FcγR 结合并降低 ADCD 活性和 IgM 水平。最后,母乳中的基线 ADCD 活性和血清 IgG1 水平被确定为生命前六个月对流感感染抵抗力的标志。与单独的任一隔室相比,结合牛奶和血清隔室的保护相关性的多变量模型提供了更大的预测能力,这表明抗体转移的两种途径都增强了婴儿的抗流感免疫力。这些数据共同表明,母体流感 疫苗接种 通过母乳赋予婴儿保护,以增强胎盘抗体转移,并且这些保护性抗体的功能能力可以通过延长母乳喂养而增强。

title: The roles of pre-season immunity, age, viral shedding, and community exposures in shaping influenza household transmission dynamics
abstract: Abstract Our understanding of influenza transmission remains imperfect due to the high prevalence of asymptomatic infections that often go undetected. To address this challenge, we leveraged uniquely resolved data from a household cohort study spanning three consecutive years in rural and urban South Africa. The study incorporated pre-season serum collection and twice-weekly virological testing during the influenza season, regardless of symptom presence. We developed a subtype/lineage-specific influenza household transmission model that accounts for time-resolved viral shedding across the full clinical spectrum of infections, allowing us to disentangle the role of household and community exposures, pre-season immunity, and age on transmission. Our analysis revealed that viral shedding intensity, as measured by the cycle threshold (Ct) values of infected household members, significantly correlated with the risk of transmission for all four influenza subtypes/lineages. After adjusting for viral shedding, pre-season hemagglutination inhibition (HAI) titers greater than 1:40 were associated with a significantly lower risk of infection acquisition for A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B/Victoria, but not for B/Yamagata. Notably, children exhibited higher susceptibility and longer viral shedding durations compared to adults across all subtypes/lineages, even after adjusting for pre-season HAI titers. While our findings support that HAI titers correlate with protection, the strong residual effects of age on susceptibility and viral shedding may reflect the accumulation of additional immune responses shaped by repeated exposures over time. Our study underscores the need to explore immune mechanisms beyond HAI titers that modulate influenza susceptibility and transmission.

title_zh: 季前免疫力、年龄、病毒脱落和社区暴露在塑造流感家庭 传播 动态中的作用
source_body_en: Abstract Our understanding of influenza transmission remains imperfect due to the high prevalence of asymptomatic infections that often go undetected. To address this challenge, we leveraged uniquely resolved data from a household cohort study spanning three consecutive years in rural and urban South Africa. The study incorporated pre-season serum collection and twice-weekly virological testing during the influenza season, regardless of symptom presence. We developed a subtype/lineage-specific influenza household transmission model that accounts for time-resolved viral shedding across the full clinical spectrum of infections, allowing us to disentangle the role of household and community exposures, pre-season immunity, and age on transmission. Our analysis revealed that viral shedding intensity, as measured by the cycle threshold (Ct) values of infected household members, significantly correlated with the risk of transmission for all four influenza subtypes/lineages. After adjusting for viral shedding, pre-season hemagglutination inhibition (HAI) titers greater than 1:40 were associated with a significantly lower risk of infection acquisition for A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B/Victoria, but not for B/Yamagata. Notably, children exhibited higher susceptibility and longer viral shedding durations compared to adults across all subtypes/lineages, even after adjusting for pre-season HAI titers. While our findings support that HAI titers correlate with protection, the strong residual effects of age on susceptibility and viral shedding may reflect the accumulation of additional immune responses shaped by repeated exposures over time. Our study underscores the need to explore immune mechanisms beyond HAI titers that modulate influenza susceptibility and transmission.
abstract_zh: 摘要:我们对流感传播的理解仍然不完善,因为无症状感染的高患病率常常未被检测到。为应对这一挑战,我们利用了来自南非农村和城市地区连续三年的家庭队列研究研究中独特解析的数据。该研究纳入了季前血清采集和流感季节期间每周两次的病毒学检测,无论是否存在症状。我们开发了一种亚型/谱系特异性的流感家庭传播模型,该模型考虑了整个感染临床谱中的时间解析病毒脱落,使我们能够分离家庭和社区暴露、季前免疫力和年龄对传播的影响。我们的分析显示,受感染家庭成员的病毒脱落强度,以循环阈值(Ct)值衡量,与所有四种流感亚型/谱系的传播风险显著相关。在调整病毒脱落后,季前血凝抑制(HAI)滴度大于1:40与甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09、甲型H3N2流感病毒和B/Victoria的感染获取风险显著降低相关,但对B/Yamagata则无此关联。值得注意的是,与成人相比,儿童在所有亚型/谱系中表现出更高的易感性和更长的病毒脱落持续时间,即使在调整了季前HAI滴度后也是如此。虽然我们的研究结果支持HAI滴度与保护作用相关,但年龄对易感性和病毒脱落的强烈残余效应可能反映了随时间推移反复暴露所形成的额外免疫应答的积累。我们的研究强调了需要探索超出HAI滴度的免疫机制,这些机制调节流感的易感性和传播。

title: Development, applications, and future prospects of RNA virus reverse genetics technology
abstract: Viral reverse genetics enables the rescue of infectious virions from cloned cDNA and serves as a core technique for mapping viral genotype–phenotype relationships, dissecting RNA viral life cycles, and developing antiviral countermeasures. This review systematically summarizes the evolution, technical framework and optimization strategies of RNA virus reverse genetics, with three prototype viruses covering all major RNA genome types: SARS-CoV-2 (+ssRNA), non-segmented negative-sense Newcastle disease virus (NDV), and segmented negative-sense influenza A virus. Core modules including infectious clone construction, diverse promoter systems, hammerhead/HDV ribozymes, and solutions for large unstable genomes such as BAC and ISA are elaborated. We summarize its irreplaceable applications in vaccine development, pathogenesis research, virus-host interaction analysis and high-throughput antiviral screening. Current bottlenecks include low rescue efficiency, cDNA genetic instability and biosafety hazards. We also introduce non-infectious surrogate platforms and establish a three-tier antiviral screening pipeline. Future advances will integrate CRISPR/Cas editing, standardized modular tools, biosafety engineering, AI and big data. Distinct from previous reviews focusing on single viral genera, this work conducts cross-type horizontal comparisons and summarizes universal technical obstacles and tailored optimizations, offering comprehensive references for basic virology, accelerated vaccine innovation and precise antiviral design.

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on RNA virus reverse genetics technology, covering its development, applications, and future prospects. analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a systematic review that summarizes the evolution, technical framework, and optimization strategies of RNA virus reverse genetics. It uses three prototype viruses representing all major RNA genome types: SARS-CoV-2 (+ssRNA), Newcastle disease virus (NDV), and influenza A virus. The review elaborates on core modules such as infectious clone construction, promoter systems, ribozymes, and solutions for large unstable genomes.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The consensus is that RNA virus reverse genetics is an irreplaceable tool for vaccine development, pathogenesis research, virus-host interaction analysis, and high-throughput antiviral screening. The review highlights its applications across different RNA virus types and emphasizes its importance in basic virology, vaccine innovation, and antiviral design.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Current bottlenecks include low rescue efficiency, cDNA genetic instability, and biosafety hazards. The review identifies these as key challenges that need to be addressed to advance the field. analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: Future advances should integrate CRISPR/Cas editing, standardized modular tools, biosafety engineering, AI, and big data to improve the efficiency and safety of RNA virus reverse genetics. title_zh: RNA病毒反向遗传学技术的发展、应用及未来展望
source_body_en: Viral reverse genetics enables the rescue of infectious virions from cloned cDNA and serves as a core technique for mapping viral genotype–phenotype relationships, dissecting RNA viral life cycles, and developing antiviral countermeasures. This review systematically summarizes the evolution, technical framework and optimization strategies of RNA virus reverse genetics, with three prototype viruses covering all major RNA genome types: SARS-CoV-2 (+ssRNA), non-segmented negative-sense Newcastle disease virus (NDV), and segmented negative-sense influenza A virus. Core modules including infectious clone construction, diverse promoter systems, hammerhead/HDV ribozymes, and solutions for large unstable genomes such as BAC and ISA are elaborated. We summarize its irreplaceable applications in vaccine development, pathogenesis research, virus-host interaction analysis and high-throughput antiviral screening. Current bottlenecks include low rescue efficiency, cDNA genetic instability and biosafety hazards. We also introduce non-infectious surrogate platforms and establish a three-tier antiviral screening pipeline. Future advances will integrate CRISPR/Cas editing, standardized modular tools, biosafety engineering, AI and big data. Distinct from previous reviews focusing on single viral genera, this work conducts cross-type horizontal comparisons and summarizes universal technical obstacles and tailored optimizations, offering comprehensive references for basic virology, accelerated vaccine innovation and precise antiviral design.

title: Original Paper The influence of early influenza exposures on immunity in infants and children: The US Influenza IMPRINT Cohort (Preprint)
abstract: BACKGROUND Influenza vaccine effectiveness is variable, while influenza morbidity and mortality remain high. Immunologic imprinting for influenza has been described and may contribute to suboptimal vaccine performance. Unfortunately, critical data are lacking on the natural history of influenza in pregnancy and childhood. Appropriately designed maternal-birth cohorts can identify the earliest exposures to influenza and are necessary to address gaps in influenza epidemiology and immunology that currently hinder our ability to develop more broadly effective and durable vaccines. OBJECTIVE We describe the protocol for the Influenza IMPRINT Cohort (Immunological Memory to Prior INfluenza over Time), an intensive maternal-birth cohort, which aims to understand how early exposures to influenza antigens shape responses later in life. METHODS IMPRINT is a prospective birth cohort of healthy mothers and children in Cincinnati, Ohio. Mothers are enrolled in the third trimester and followed with their child for at least three years with an enrollment goal of 1,500 mother-child pairs. Starting in week 2 of life, weekly child nasal swabs and twice weekly symptom surveys are collected, regardless of the presence/absence of symptoms. Serum is collected from mothers at enrollment and each summer post-enrollment. Child blood samples are collected from the umbilical cord at delivery and from the child at week 6, every summer, and following influenza infection and vaccination. Whole blood, serum, plasma, and peripheral blood mononucleated cells are collected. Medical records are abstracted to capture clinical data on medically attended respiratory illness. Review of state registries and the medical record capture vaccine administration dates. Other collected specimens included stool, human milk, saliva, and cheek swabs. Epidemiologic, immunologic, and virologic studies are underway to determine how influenza exposures influence incidence, subclinical infection, symptomology, and immunologic responses to subsequent exposures. RESULTS Screening and enrollment began October 2019 and ended November 2025. In total, 1,624 mothers were provisionally enrolled in pregnancy and 1,324 met final eligibility criteria for study enrollment. Participant follow-up is on-going. Participants that met final eligibility requirements were significantly different from those that did not; enrolled mothers tended to be older, in a partnership, of white race and/or non-Hispanic ethnicity, have private insurance, higher household income, and more education. CONCLUSIONS IMPRINT integrates advanced methodologic, laboratory, and epidemiologic tools from a complimentary group of collaborators to detect and order influenza infections and vaccinations experienced in the first years of life. This cohort struggled to advance maternal-infant pairs through the eligibility run-in period but also demonstrated successful follow-up of those pairs that met eligibility in an intensive, multi-year study. IMPRINT provides a novel framework to improve understanding of the immunologic responses to primary influenza exposures and to describe how the initial exposure and the subsequent order of exposures impacts the influenza immune landscape. CLINICALTRIAL ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT05436184

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 背景流感 疫苗 的有效性是可变的,而流感发病率和 疫苗 仍然很高。流感的免疫印记已被描述,并且可能导致 疫苗 性能不佳。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: IMPRINT 是俄亥俄州辛辛那提市健康母亲和儿童的预产期 队列研究。母亲在妊娠晚期进行登记,并对其孩子进行至少三年的跟踪,登记目标为 1,500 对母子。

title_zh: 原始论文早期流感暴露对婴儿和儿童免疫力的影响:美国流感 IMPRINT 队列研究(预印本)
source_body_en: BACKGROUND Influenza vaccine effectiveness is variable, while influenza morbidity and mortality remain high. Immunologic imprinting for influenza has been described and may contribute to suboptimal vaccine performance. Unfortunately, critical data are lacking on the natural history of influenza in pregnancy and childhood. Appropriately designed maternal-birth cohorts can identify the earliest exposures to influenza and are necessary to address gaps in influenza epidemiology and immunology that currently hinder our ability to develop more broadly effective and durable vaccines. OBJECTIVE We describe the protocol for the Influenza IMPRINT Cohort (Immunological Memory to Prior INfluenza over Time), an intensive maternal-birth cohort, which aims to understand how early exposures to influenza antigens shape responses later in life. METHODS IMPRINT is a prospective birth cohort of healthy mothers and children in Cincinnati, Ohio. Mothers are enrolled in the third trimester and followed with their child for at least three years with an enrollment goal of 1,500 mother-child pairs. Starting in week 2 of life, weekly child nasal swabs and twice weekly symptom surveys are collected, regardless of the presence/absence of symptoms. Serum is collected from mothers at enrollment and each summer post-enrollment. Child blood samples are collected from the umbilical cord at delivery and from the child at week 6, every summer, and following influenza infection and vaccination. Whole blood, serum, plasma, and peripheral blood mononucleated cells are collected. Medical records are abstracted to capture clinical data on medically attended respiratory illness. Review of state registries and the medical record capture vaccine administration dates. Other collected specimens included stool, human milk, saliva, and cheek swabs. Epidemiologic, immunologic, and virologic studies are underway to determine how influenza exposures influence incidence, subclinical infection, symptomology, and immunologic responses to subsequent exposures. RESULTS Screening and enrollment began October 2019 and ended November 2025. In total, 1,624 mothers were provisionally enrolled in pregnancy and 1,324 met final eligibility criteria for study enrollment. Participant follow-up is on-going. Participants that met final eligibility requirements were significantly different from those that did not; enrolled mothers tended to be older, in a partnership, of white race and/or non-Hispanic ethnicity, have private insurance, higher household income, and more education. CONCLUSIONS IMPRINT integrates advanced methodologic, laboratory, and epidemiologic tools from a complimentary group of collaborators to detect and order influenza infections and vaccinations experienced in the first years of life. This cohort struggled to advance maternal-infant pairs through the eligibility run-in period but also demonstrated successful follow-up of those pairs that met eligibility in an intensive, multi-year study. IMPRINT provides a novel framework to improve understanding of the immunologic responses to primary influenza exposures and to describe how the initial exposure and the subsequent order of exposures impacts the influenza immune landscape. CLINICALTRIAL ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT05436184
abstract_zh: 背景流感 疫苗 的有效性是可变的,而流感发病率和 疫苗 仍然很高。流感的免疫印记已被描述,并且可能导致 疫苗 性能不佳。不幸的是,缺乏关于妊娠期和儿童期流感自然史的关键数据。适当设计的产妇出生 队列研究 可以识别最早的流感暴露,并且对于解决流感 流行病学 和免疫学方面的差距是必要的,这些差距目前阻碍了我们开发更广泛有效和持久的 疫苗 的能力。目的 我们描述了流感 IMPRINT 队列研究(对先前流感随时间的免疫记忆)的方案,这是一种强化产妇分娩 队列研究,旨在了解早期接触流感抗原如何影响以后生活的反应。方法 IMPRINT 是俄亥俄州辛辛那提市健康母亲和儿童的预产期 队列研究。母亲在妊娠晚期进行登记,并对其孩子进行至少三年的跟踪,登记目标为 1,500 对母子。从出生后第 2 周开始,无论是否存在症状,每周都会收集儿童鼻拭子和每周两次的症状调查。在入学时和入学后的每年夏天从母亲那里收集血清。每年夏天,以及流感感染和 疫苗接种 后,从分娩时的脐带和第 6 周的儿童采集儿童血样。收集全血、血清、血浆和外周血单核细胞。提取医疗记录以获取就医呼吸系统疾病的临床数据。审查国家登记处和医疗记录以获取 疫苗 给药日期。其他收集的样本包括粪便、母乳、唾液和脸颊拭子。流行病学、免疫学和病毒学研究正在进行中,以确定流感暴露如何影响 发病率、亚临床感染、症状学和对后续暴露的免疫反应。结果 筛选和入组开始于 2019 年 10 月,结束于 2025 年 11 月。总共有 1,624 名怀孕母亲临时入组,其中 1,324 名母亲符合研究入组的最终资格标准。参与者的后续行动正在进行中。满足最终资格要求的参与者与未满足最终资格要求的参与者存在显着差异;登记的母亲往往年龄较大,有伴侣,是白人和/或非西班牙裔,有私人保险,家庭收入较高,受教育程度较高。结论 IMPRINT 整合了来自一组互补合作者的先进方法、实验室和流行病学工具,以检测和订购流感感染以及生命第一年经历的 疫苗接种。队列研究 努力在资格磨合期促进母婴对的发展,但也在一项深入的多年研究中成功地跟踪了那些符合资格的母婴对。IMPRINT 提供了一个新的框架,以提高对初次流感暴露的免疫反应的理解,并描述初始暴露和随后的暴露顺序如何影响流感免疫景观。临床试验 ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT05436184

title: Patterns of the gut microbiota and metabolome as potential biomarkers associated with influenza vaccine immunogenicity in systemic lupus erythematosus: a cross-sectional observational pilot study
abstract: Immunogenicity to influenza vaccination is often impaired in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). The role of the gut microbiota and its metabolic output in modulating this response remains underexplored. This study is the first to explore gut microbiota patterns and metabolites in response to influenza vaccination in patients with SLE. A cross-sectional observational pilot study was conducted at Ramathibodi Hospital between May 2021 and July 2022. Participants with SLE who had received either a boosted dose or a standard dose of a quadrivalent influenza vaccine were enrolled. We analyzed fecal 16 S rDNA and metabolomic profiles using liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry to identify signatures associated with seroconversion (determined using the hemagglutination inhibition assay). A total of 62 participants with SLE participated in the study, and 61 fecal samples were submitted for metabolomic analysis. Most participants were female (58/62, 93.6%). The median ages in the standard and booster dose groups were 35.5 (interquartile range 28–42.5) and 34 (25–43) years, respectively ( P = 0.878). The overall gut microbiota patterns were similar in both groups; however, the genus Bacteroides was significantly associated with seroconversion to A(H1N1) and A(H3N2) ( P < 0.05). Metabolomic analysis identified upregulation of 1,5-anhydro-D-glucitol and L-cysteic acid in seroconverters, whereas neopterin was significantly elevated in nonresponders, furthermore, several bacterial taxa were correlated with these metabolites. The level of immunosuppressive treatment and the use of antimicrobials for prophylaxis against opportunistic infections affected influenza immunogenicity in this study population. Some metabolites also appeared to be linked to vaccine immunogenicity, although the underlying mechanism is unclear. Our findings identify specific gut microbial taxa and fecal metabolites, particularly 1,5-anhydro-D-glucitol, which are significantly associated with influenza vaccine immunogenicity in SLE patients. These results suggest that the gut–immune axis may play a modulatory role in vaccine responses and may provide potential non-invasive biomarkers that can identify patients at risk of suboptimal influenza protection.

Conducted at Ramathibodi Hospital with 62 SLE patients, the study analyzed fecal samples using 16 S rDNA sequencing and metabolomics. title_zh: 肠道微生物群和代谢组的模式作为与系统性红斑狼疮中流感 疫苗 免疫原性相关的潜在生物标志物:横断面观察性试点研究
source_body_en: Immunogenicity to influenza vaccination is often impaired in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). The role of the gut microbiota and its metabolic output in modulating this response remains underexplored. This study is the first to explore gut microbiota patterns and metabolites in response to influenza vaccination in patients with SLE. A cross-sectional observational pilot study was conducted at Ramathibodi Hospital between May 2021 and July 2022. Participants with SLE who had received either a boosted dose or a standard dose of a quadrivalent influenza vaccine were enrolled. We analyzed fecal 16 S rDNA and metabolomic profiles using liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry to identify signatures associated with seroconversion (determined using the hemagglutination inhibition assay). A total of 62 participants with SLE participated in the study, and 61 fecal samples were submitted for metabolomic analysis. Most participants were female (58/62, 93.6%). The median ages in the standard and booster dose groups were 35.5 (interquartile range 28–42.5) and 34 (25–43) years, respectively ( P = 0.878). The overall gut microbiota patterns were similar in both groups; however, the genus Bacteroides was significantly associated with seroconversion to A(H1N1) and A(H3N2) ( P < 0.05). Metabolomic analysis identified upregulation of 1,5-anhydro-D-glucitol and L-cysteic acid in seroconverters, whereas neopterin was significantly elevated in nonresponders, furthermore, several bacterial taxa were correlated with these metabolites. The level of immunosuppressive treatment and the use of antimicrobials for prophylaxis against opportunistic infections affected influenza immunogenicity in this study population. Some metabolites also appeared to be linked to vaccine immunogenicity, although the underlying mechanism is unclear. Our findings identify specific gut microbial taxa and fecal metabolites, particularly 1,5-anhydro-D-glucitol, which are significantly associated with influenza vaccine immunogenicity in SLE patients. These results suggest that the gut–immune axis may play a modulatory role in vaccine responses and may provide potential non-invasive biomarkers that can identify patients at risk of suboptimal influenza protection.

title: Descriptive epidemiology and economic impact of highly pathogenic avian influenza in Plateau State, Nigeria: a retrospect from 2015 to 2022
abstract: In 2006, millions of poultry mortality was associated with high pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) in Nigeria. The disease was brought under control from 2008 to 2014, then a resurgence in 2015. This study therefore aimed at investigating the occurrence, locations and seasonal conditions that facilitated HPAI outbreak and estimate its related economic losses in Plateau State, Nigeria, from 2015 to 2022.vThe HPAI data used were reported cases recorded by the Avian Influenza Desk office, Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, Plateau State. Number of farms, flock size, type of birds, year of cases reported and laboratory results as well as seasons of spread of the disease were extracted and utilized for this study. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and zero inflated negative binomial for trend analysis. The highest number of HPAI cases was recorded in 2015, with 151 cases, accounting for 52.6 % of the total reported cases while the lowest number of cases was in 2019 with only two cases, representing 0.7% of the total cases. The peak prevalence occurred between February and March of the period of study, with a decline thereafter until December. Jos South LGAs had the highest number of positive results, followed by Jos North, while Mangu, Barkin-Ladi, and Wase LGAs had the lowest. An estimated loss of 130,481,135 eggs from a total mortality of 825,000 poultry birds in 304 farms translates to a cumulative economic loss of ₦ 6,023,401,525.00 ($ 4,068,441.94.00). The distribution of HPAI varied across different LGAs of the State. The study provided valuable insights into the epidemiology and the direct or indirect huge economic losses due to HPAI in Plateau State, Nigeria.
journal: Proceedings of the Nigerian Academy of Science

title: Activating laboratory surveillance response to the threat of H5N1 influenza in the Veterans Health Administration, 2024–25
abstract: Introduction The Veterans Health Administration (VHA) mobilized and adapted its established national infrastructure to enhance influenza surveillance during 2024–2025 highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) A(H5N1) panzootic. Additionally, VHA's Public Health Reference Laboratory (PHRL) expanded capacity for H5 subtyping and whole genome sequencing (WGS) to support detection. Methods Routine influenza surveillance was enhanced with customized queries to identify cases in high-risk counties with reported H5N1 detected in animals. In coordination with VHA clinical laboratories, select samples were sent to PHRL. PHRL subtyped specimens received, which included hospitalized cases. Demographics of influenza A cases in VHA were compared with those residing in high-risk “surveilled” counties (with reported H5N1 detection in animals) and those whose specimens were sent to PHRL for H5 subtyping. Results From 4/1/2024-5/31/2025, we identified 40,406 positive influenza A VHA cases (12.5% with local subtyping performed), including 5,348 cases from “surveilled” counties. A total of 1,155 specimens were received by PHRL for H5 subtyping and 180 completed WGS. Cases from “surveilled” counties had fewer females, fewer in 50–69 age group and more of Hispanic ethnicity compared to other influenza A cases. No H5N1 was detected. Conclusion We highlight the complexity and resources necessary for epidemiologic and laboratory surveillance of H5N1 within a large, national health system during a recognized panzootic. Additional resources for decentralized influenza A subtyping at local VA clinical laboratories are needed as centralized subtyping and WGS at PHRL was not comprehensive. Although H5 influenza has not yet been observed among Veterans within VHA, the ongoing risk warrants continued vigilance and monitoring.

title: Genetic and Pathogenicity Studies of Avian Influenza (H9N2) Virus Isolated from Chickens in Jiangsu Province, China, in 2025
abstract: In this study, one H9N2 subtype avian influenza virus (AIV) was isolated in Jiangsu Province, China, in March 2025. According to phylogenetic analysis, the HA gene fragment of the H9N2 isolate was classified as the B4.7 lineage, with the remaining seven segments falling into the Eurasian lineage. This H9N2 virus underwent complex genetic reassortment across multiple regions in China during its evolution, and key amino acid substitutions were identified, which may enhance its viral polymerase activity and replication efficiency in mice. Critically, a mouse experiment demonstrated that the H9N2 virus replicated effectively in the lungs and nasal turbinates of BALB/c mice without requiring prior adaptation. In addition, poultry infection studies showed that the H9N2 virus could replicate and spread more efficiently in chickens than in ducks. Moreover, the virus could be transmitted to contacted ducks through infected chickens with greater efficiency than from ducks to ducks. Furthermore, in the lungs of inoculated chickens and ducks, the mRNA expression levels of pattern-recognition receptors (PRRs) and cytokines were upregulated, while the overall fold increase in ducks was lower than that in chickens. In conclusion, these results highlighted the potential public health risk presented by chicken-derived H9N2 AIV, emphasizing the critical need for enhanced routine surveillance of H9N2 AIVs from poultry.

title: Analysis of the pathogen spectrum, co-infection characteristics, and risk of severe disease in community-acquired pneumonia among children in Henan province
abstract: Objective To analyze the pathogen spectrum, co-infection characteristics, and risk factors for severe pneumonia in children with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) in Henan Province. Methods This study included 2,149 pediatric inpatients with CAP admitted to the Third Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University from June 2023 to June 2025. Throat swab samples were tested using multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for 11 respiratory pathogens. Combined with culture results, the pathogen spectrum and co-infection characteristics were analyzed, and risk factors for severe pneumonia were identified using multivariate logistic regression analysis. It should be noted that a positive throat-swab PCR result cannot unambiguously differentiate pathogenic infection from colonization, prior infection, or asymptomatic carriage; this inherent limitation was taken into account during data interpretation. Results The overall pathogen detection rate was 89.34%, with Mycoplasma pneumoniae (31.55%) and rhinovirus (31.13%) predominating; among bacteria, Haemophilus influenzae (3.77%) and Streptococcus pneumoniae (3.35%) were the most common. Except for influenza B virus and human coronavirus, significant differences were observed in the age distribution of each pathogen ( P < 0.05). The detection rate of M. pneumoniae increased significantly with age, reaching 58.5% in school-aged children. Rhinovirus was active throughout the year (peaking at 65.14% in October 2024), while M. pneumoniae had the highest detection rate in October 2023 (65.93%). The overall co-infection rate was 31.07%, consisting primarily of virus–virus or virus–atypical pathogen combinations (21.49%), with rhinovirus– M. pneumoniae being the most common (8.52%). abstract_zh: 目的分析河南省社区获得性肺炎(CAP)儿童重症肺炎的病原谱、合并感染特征及危险因素。方法本研究纳入2023年6月至2025年6月郑州大学第三附属医院收治的2149名CAP儿科住院患者,采用多重聚合酶链反应(PCR)对咽拭子样本进行11种呼吸道病原体检测。结合培养结果,分析病原谱和合并感染特征,并采用多元Logistic回归分析确定重症肺炎的危险因素。值得注意的是,咽拭子 PCR 阳性结果不能明确区分病原体感染与定植、既往感染或无症状携带;在数据解释过程中考虑到了这种固有的局限性。结果病原菌总体检出率为89.34%,以肺炎支原体(31.55%)和鼻病毒(31.13%)为主;细菌中,流感嗜血杆菌(3.77%)和肺炎链球菌(3.35%)最为常见。除乙型流感病毒和人类冠状病毒外,各病原体的年龄分布均存在显着差异( P < 0.05)。肺炎支原体检出率随着年龄的增长而显着升高,学龄儿童中肺炎支原体检出率达到58.5%。鼻病毒全年活跃(2024年10月达到峰值65.14%),而肺炎支原体检出率最高的是2023年10月(65.93%)。总体混合感染率为31.07%,主要由病毒-病毒或病毒-非典型病原体组合组成(21.49%),其中鼻病毒-肺炎支原体最为常见(8.52%)。重症肺炎的独立危险因素是基础疾病(OR = 4.031)和早产史(OR = 3.544),而病毒或非典型病原体合并感染或并发细菌感染并不会显着增加重症风险。结论 2023年6月至2025年6月,河南省儿童CAP病原谱以肺炎支原体和鼻病毒为主(HRV阳性无症状携带率较高,需谨慎解读),年龄分布明显。基础疾病和早产史是重症肺炎的主要危险因素。

title: Genetic determinants of cell- and egg-preferred replication in H3N2 canine influenza virus
abstract: The H3N2 canine influenza virus (CIV), which originated from avian influenza viruses and has circulated in dogs for over two decades, remains poorly understood in terms of its host adaptation mechanisms and cellular tropism. In this study, we isolated two phenotypically distinct H3N2 CIV strains (CX3 and CX12) from a canine respiratory disease outbreak. Although both were isolated using MDCK cells, CX3 showed higher replication efficiency and plaque-forming ability in MDCK cells, whereas CX12 replicated more efficiently in chicken embryos. Using reverse genetics, we identified the PB1 gene as a critical enhancer of viral polymerase activity and the HA gene as a key contributor to viral stability, both of which collectively mediate cell-preferred replication. These findings provide mechanistic insights into H3N2 CIV host adaptation and offer a foundation for future vaccine development.

title: High-efficiency upconversion luminescent quenching via defect-engineered Cu 3− x P for dual-aptamers-mediated tri-modal H1N1 lateral flow immunoassay
abstract: Abstract Early diagnosis of Influenza A virus is critical for influenza prevention and control by reducing severe illness and mortality. However, conventional lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA) is limited by low sensitivity, and luminescent LFIA is short of significant signal changes at low target concentrations. Herein, a luminescence quenching LFIA platform is developed by integrating upconversion nanoparticles, defect engineered Cu3−xP, and dual aptamers to address above bottleneck via a synergistic mechanism. Density functional theory calculations indicate that in the new type Cu3−xP quencher, Cu vacancies induce new electronic states at the valence band edge and create extra electron transition pathway, which boost Förster Resonance Energy Transfer and upconversion luminescence quenching efficiency. Cu3−xP also exhibits broad ultraviolet–visible (UV–vis) absorption for colorimetric and photothermal signals. Moreover, two selected aptamers with stable and non-overlapping binding sites verified by molecular docking are critical for forming a sandwich structure, enabling high sensitivity toward H1N1 over H7N9, H9N2, H6N1, H7N7, and H5N1, along with good anti-interference ability. This work provides a scalable point of care influenza detection strategy balancing sensitivity and specificity, optimizing LFIA for on site viral diagnostics.

abstract_zh: 摘要 甲型流感病毒的早期 诊断 对于减少重症和 诊断 流感预防和控制至关重要。然而,传统的侧流免疫分析(LFIA)由于灵敏度低而受到限制,而发光LFIA在低目标浓度下缺乏显着的信号变化。在此,通过集成上转换纳米粒子、缺陷工程 Cu3−xP 和双适体,开发了发光猝灭 LFIA 平台,以通过协同机制解决上述瓶颈。密度泛函理论计算表明,在新型 Cu3−xP 猝灭剂中,Cu 空位在价带边缘诱导新的电子态并产生额外的电子跃迁路径,从而提高福斯特共振能量转移和上转换发光猝灭效率。因此,有效抑制测试线发光信号,建立灵敏的发光猝灭LFIA,对信号变化敏感。Cu3−xP 还对色度和光热信号表现出广泛的紫外可见 (UV-vis) 吸收。协同发光-比色-光热三模式分析平台实现了 H1N1 血凝素的检测限为 0.907 ng/mL。此外,通过分子对接验证的两个具有稳定且不重叠结合位点的适配体对于形成夹心结构至关重要,使得对H1N1的敏感性高于H7N9、H9N2、H6N1、H7N7和H5N1,并且具有良好的抗干扰能力。这项工作提供了一种可扩展的护理点流感检测策略,平衡了灵敏度和特异性,优化了 LFIA 进行现场病毒诊断。

title: Analysis of Influenza A viruses using the resonant recognition model
abstract: Bird flu (Avian influenza) and human flu are both caused by Influenza A viruses, but they differ significantly in their host adaptation, transmission and severity. Here, we have used the Resonant Recognition Model (RRM), which is innovative approach using knowledge from quantum physics, biochemistry and mathematics, capable to analyse interactions between proteins and their targets, including other proteins, DNA, RNA, or small molecules. Using the RRM model we have identified different characteristics for different types of flu viruses, and we have found that there are three groups of flu viruses with completely different interactions with host cells receptors. Such finding can provide explanation why different flu viruses can interact only with specific hosts and why there is extremely low cross infection between different species, in particular between birds and humans.
journal: International Journal of Science and Research Archive

full_text: Abstract Antibody responses to seasonal influenza vaccination are shaped by immune history, but the effects of prior vaccination frequency and recency on standard serological endpoints remain incompletely defined. We analyzed paired pre- and post-vaccination hemagglutination inhibition and neuraminidase inhibition titers from 775 adults in the New Zealand SHIVERS-II cohort during the 2018 influenza season and related these to vaccination histories (2013–2017). Post-vaccination titers increased across groups, but participants vaccinated more frequently were less likely to meet conventional ≥4-fold rise and seroconversion criteria, particularly for A/H3N2. Notably, these lower probabilities occurred despite higher absolute post-vaccination titers among frequently vaccinated participants. Longer intervals since the most recent vaccination were associated with higher probabilities of meeting these thresholds; neuraminidase responses showed similar patterns. Pre-vaccination titers were strongly correlated with post-vaccination titers and inversely associated with fold-rise magnitude. These findings indicate that vaccination frequency and recency shape measured humoral responses and highlight that fold-rise-based immunogenicity metrics should be interpreted in the context of baseline immunity and immune history. Despite lower fold rise responses in some groups, most participants showed measurable increases in HAI and NAI titers following vaccination, consistent with ongoing immunologic recall; these serologic findings should not be interpreted as evidence of reduced clinical protection, which was not assessed in this study. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate how vaccination history, including frequency and recency, influences humoral responses to seasonal influenza vaccination, as these effects on standard serological endpoints were incompletely defined.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We analyzed paired pre- and post-vaccination hemagglutination inhibition and neuraminidase inhibition titers from 775 adults in the New Zealand SHIVERS-II cohort during the 2018 influenza season, relating these to vaccination histories from 2013–2017.
analysis.methods: Paired pre- and post-vaccination hemagglutination inhibition and neuraminidase inhibition titers were analyzed and related to vaccination histories (2013–2017) to assess immunogenicity metrics.
analysis.main_results: Post-vaccination titers increased across groups, but participants vaccinated more frequently were less likely to meet conventional ≥4-fold rise and seroconversion criteria, particularly for A/H3N2, despite higher absolute post-vaccination titers; longer intervals since the most recent vaccination were associated with higher probabilities of meeting these thresholds.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that vaccination frequency and recency shape measured humoral responses, highlighting that fold-rise-based immunogenicity metrics should be interpreted in the context of baseline immunity and immune history, which was a novel insight for understanding serological responses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings inform that immunogenicity metrics should be interpreted considering vaccination history, which is crucial for evaluating vaccine efficacy and guiding vaccination strategies, though clinical protection was not assessed.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study did not assess clinical protection, limiting direct public health implications; however, the large sample size and robust serological methods provide moderate evidence strength for the observed immunological patterns.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated how vaccination history influences humoral responses to seasonal influenza vaccination in 775 New Zealand adults. Analyzing paired pre- and post-vaccination titers from 2018, researchers found that more frequent vaccination was associated with lower probabilities of meeting conventional seroconversion criteria, despite higher absolute post-vaccination titers, particularly for A/H3N2. Longer intervals since recent vaccination correlated with better serological responses. The findings highlight that fold-rise metrics must be interpreted in the context of baseline immunity and vaccination history, though clinical protection was not assessed. This provides important insights for evaluating vaccine immunogenicity and informing vaccination strategies.

abstract_zh: 我们分析了 2018 年流感季期间新西兰 SHIVERS-II 队列研究 中 775 名成年人的配对前后 疫苗接种 血凝抑制和神经氨酸酶抑制滴度,并将这些与 疫苗接种 历史(2013-2017 年)相关联。这些发现表明,疫苗接种 频率和新近形状测量了体液反应,并强调基于倍数上升的免疫原性指标应在基线免疫和免疫史的背景下进行解释。尽管某些组的倍数上升反应较低,但大多数参与者在 疫苗接种 后表现出 HAI 和 NAI 滴度可测量的增加,这与正在进行的免疫记忆一致;这些血清学结果不应被解释为临床保护减少的证据,本研究未对此进行评估。摘要:对 季节性流感 疫苗接种 的抗体反应由免疫史决定,但之前的 疫苗接种 频率和新近度对标准血清学终点的影响仍未完全确定。疫苗接种 后各组的滴度有所增加,但接种频率较高的参与者不太可能满足传统的 ≥4 倍上升和血清转换标准,特别是 A/H3N2。值得注意的是,尽管经常接种疫苗的参与者在 疫苗接种 后的绝对滴度较高,但这些较低的概率还是发生了。自最近的 疫苗接种 以来的较长间隔与满足这些阈值的较高概率相关;神经氨酸酶反应显示出相似的模式。疫苗接种 前的滴度与 疫苗接种 后的滴度密切相关,并且与倍数上升幅度呈负相关。受试者致谢 我们感谢 SHIVERS-II 调查小组的成员 Jacqui Ralston6、Judy Bocacao6、Jessica Danielewicz8、Wendy...

title: Newton Divided Difference Optimization for Fingerprint-Based Neural Virtual Screening against Avian Influenza A/H9N2
abstract: Avian influenza A/H9N2 poses persistent zoonotic and veterinary threats, yet efficient computational tools for antiviral compound prioritization remain underdeveloped, particularly with respect to optimizer behavior in high-dimensional neural screening. This study proposes Newton Divided Difference (NDD) optimization, a lightweight positive diagonal curvature-aware training strategy, as a novel optimizer for fingerprint-based neural virtual screening against avian influenza A/H9N2, with the objective of evaluating its performance across aligned molecular fingerprint representations and chemically structured validation protocols. An aligned benchmark of 1,459 molecules consisting of 615 candidate active compounds and 844 decoys was represented by EState (79 features), PubChem (881 features), and Klekota–Roth (4,860 features) fingerprints, sharing identical molecule identities, labels, and split assignments. A fixed multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifier was trained with NDD and seven baseline optimizers under stratified, scaffold-key, and similarity-cluster split protocols across five repeated seeds. NDD achieved the highest descriptive ROC-AUC (Receiver Operating Characteriztic – Area Under the Curve) and PR-AUC (Precision-Recall Area Under the Curve) on Klekota–Roth fingerprints under scaffold-key and similarity-cluster protocols, and remained competitive under the stratified split with ROC-AUC of 0.9872. Architecture-sensitivity tests confirmed stable NDD performance across multiple network configurations, with ROC-AUC values ranging from 0.9876 to 0.9890. Compared with Hessian-free optimization, NDD reduced per-run runtime from approximately 50–54 seconds to approximately 8 seconds on Klekota–Roth under the same CPU-only configuration while achieving comparable ranking performance. The novelty of this work lies in the first systematic assessment of NDD for H9N2 neural virtual screening, demonstrating that positive diagonal curvature-aware scaling provides a practical, stable, and computationally efficient optimization alternative in sparse high-dimensional ligand-based screening settings, although external validation and prospective experimental confirmation remain necessary before practical antiviral prioritization.

title: Interfering with innate immunity: type I IFNs and avian influenza susceptibility
abstract: Type I interferons (IFNs) are central to early antiviral innate immunity, being produced rapidly by diverse cell types to restrict viral replication.1 The importance of type I IFNs in host defence against infections became apparent in studies of mice treated with neutralising antibodies (Ab) against type I IFN, or rendered genetically deficient for the type I IFN receptors (IFNα/βR). Infection of these mice with a wide range of viruses resulted in severe morbidity and/or mortality.2 In contrast, control of bacterial or other non-viral pathogens in IFNα/βR-deficient mice was largely intact, while infection of mice lacking the type II IFNγR with these viruses was mild.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the effect of pH on the solubilization of the influenza A viral core, addressing a gap in understanding how environmental factors influence viral structure.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved an in vitro disassembly process of influenza A virus capsids using gradient centrifugation, conducted in a controlled laboratory setting.
analysis.methods: The methods included the use of gel electrophoresis and protein staining to visualize the disassembly of the viral core under varying acidic conditions.
analysis.main_results: Gel electrophoresis and protein staining revealed the progressive disassembly of the core structure under acidic conditions, with specific patterns observed at different pH levels.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence of pH-induced structural changes in the viral core, offering a novel visualization technique for studying viral disassembly.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings contribute to the understanding of viral structural dynamics, which may inform future research on viral stability and potential therapeutic targets.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro conditions, and the evidence is based on visual observation rather than quantitative analysis, resulting in moderate confidence in the conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the effect of pH on the solubilization of the influenza A viral core through an in vitro disassembly process. Using gel electrophoresis and protein staining, the authors observed progressive structural changes under acidic conditions, providing a novel visualization method. The findings enhance understanding of viral structural dynamics, which could support future research on viral stability and therapeutic development. However, the study's reliance on in vitro conditions and visual interpretation limits the strength of the evidence, resulting in moderate confidence in the conclusions.

full_text: Lab Animal | Volume 55 | August 2026 | 285 285 https://doi.org/10.1038/s41684-026-01776-9 Research highlights lab animal Infectious disease New knockout mice for influenza research Because viruses depend on host cells for the energy and resources needed to replicate and spread, extensive research has been devoted to identifying host factors that facilitate infection. Although these studies, including numerous in vitro screens, have uncovered hundreds of human genes that may contribute to viral replication, they do not fully capture the complexity of infection in vivo. To address this limitation, a team of researchers generated a library of CRISPR-Cas9-engineered knock- out mice and used it to identify host genes that influence susceptibility to influenza A virus infection in vivo. To prioritize candidate genes for in vivo analysis, the researchers employed a multi-step screening strategy. They first compiled 386 candidate genes from a protein interactome study and a large-scale meta-analysis. After excluding genes essential for survival, they narrowed the list to 290 can- didates. Next, they conducted an siRNA-based functional screen in influenza A virus-infected mouse L929 cells, identifying 148 genes with potential roles in viral replication. From these candidates, the team successfully generated 84 knockout mouse lines. The team challenged the 84 mouse lines with a lethal dose of the mouse-adapted pan- demic influenza A(H1N1) strain MA-CA04. They monitored survival and body weight for 14 days and calculated enhanced protective efficacy (EPE) relative to wild-type (WT) controls. Using a threshold of an average EPE of at least 25% across two or more independ- ent trials, they identified 17 gene-modified lines with increased resistance to infection. Notably, several host factors exhibited sex-specific effects, revealing differences in male and female responses that were not apparent in cell culture studies. Among the strongest candidates, Arhgef28- and Lasp1-modified mice showed robust protec- tion in both sexes. Although the molecular mechanisms remain unclear, these findings provide a valuable resource of validated host targets for future antiviral therapeutic development. Alexandra Le Bras Original reference: Ueki, H. et al. analysis.research_question_and_background: Because viruses depend on host cells for replication and spread, extensive research has identified host factors that facilitate infection, but these studies do not fully capture the complexity of infection in vivo.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A team of researchers generated a library of CRISPR-Cas9-engineered knockout mice and used it to identify host genes that influence susceptibility to influenza A virus infection in vivo.
analysis.methods: They compiled 386 candidate genes from a protein interactome study and meta-analysis, narrowed the list to 290 after excluding essential genes, conducted an siRNA-based functional screen in influenza A virus-infected mouse L929 cells, and generated 84 knockout mouse lines.
analysis.main_results: After challenging the 84 mouse lines with a lethal dose of the mouse-adapted pandemic influenza A(H1N1) strain MA-CA04, they identified 17 gene-modified lines with increased resistance to infection, with Arhgef28- and Lasp1-modified mice showing robust protection in both sexes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Although the molecular mechanisms remain unclear, these findings provide a valuable resource of validated host targets for future antiviral therapeutic development and reveal sex-specific effects not apparent in cell culture studies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The identified host factors could inform the development of novel antiviral therapies and highlight the importance of considering sex-specific responses in influenza research.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence strength is moderate due to the use of a single mouse-adapted strain and the unclear molecular mechanisms, though the large-scale in vivo screening approach provides robust data.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the limitation of in vitro studies by generating a library of CRISPR-Cas9-engineered knockout mice to identify host genes influencing influenza A virus susceptibility in vivo. The researchers screened 84 mouse lines with a lethal dose of the mouse-adapted pandemic influenza A(H1N1) strain MA-CA04, identifying 17 gene-modified lines with increased resistance. Notably, Arhgef28- and Lasp1-modified mice showed robust protection in both sexes, while other factors exhibited sex-specific effects. These findings provide a valuable resource for antiviral therapeutic development, though the molecular mechanisms remain unclear. The study highlights the importance of in vivo models and sex-specific responses in influenza research.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 由于病毒依赖于 宿主 细胞进行复制和传播,因此广泛的研究已经确定了促进感染的 宿主 因子,但这些研究并未完全捕获体内感染的复杂性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一组研究人员生成了一个 CRISPR-Cas9 基因敲除小鼠文库,并用它来识别影响体内甲型流感病毒感染易感性的 宿主 基因。
elements_zh.methods: 他们从蛋白质相互作用组研究和荟萃分析中汇编了 386 个候选基因,在排除必需基因后将列表缩小到 290 个,在甲型流感病毒感染的小鼠 L929 细胞中进行了基于 siRNA 的功能筛选,并产生了 84 个敲除小鼠系。
elements_zh.main_results: 在用致死剂量的小鼠适应的甲型H1N1流行性流感病毒株MA-CA04攻击84个小鼠品系后,他们鉴定出17个基因修饰的品系具有增强的感染抵抗力,其中Arhgef28和Lasp1修饰的小鼠在两性中都显示出强大的保护作用。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 尽管分子机制仍不清楚,但这些发现为未来 宿主 治疗开发提供了经过验证的 宿主 靶标的宝贵资源,并揭示了细胞培养研究中不明显的性别特异性效应。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 确定的 宿主 因子可以为新型 抗病毒药物 疗法的开发提供信息,并强调在流感研究中考虑性别特异性反应的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 尽管大规模体内筛选方法提供了可靠的数据,但由于使用了单一的小鼠适应菌株和不清楚的分子机制,该研究的证据强度中等。

title: Xenobiotics at environmental levels modulate influenza virus replication in a lineage- and subtype-dependent manner in vitro
abstract: The influence of environmentally relevant concentrations of aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR)-active pollutants on low-pathogenic avian influenza virus (LPAIV) replication remains poorly resolved, particularly under realistic co-exposure scenarios. Here, we quantified how single and mixed AhR agonists modulate replication of multiple LPAIV subtypes in avian fibroblasts at field-relevant concentrations. Chicken (DF-1) and duck (CCL-141) fibroblasts were exposed to 9-chlorophenanthrene (0.1-50 nM), PCB126 (0.01-10 nM), and TCDD (0.001-1 nM), with or without the endogenous AhR ligand 6-formylindolo[3,2-b]carbazole (FICZ), and subsequently infected with four LPAIV subtypes (H16N3, H9N2, H7N3, H5N3). Viral replication was quantified by qPCR (ΔCt). Factorial models emphasized host lineage × virus subtype interactions and mixture-versus-single comparisons across a shared concentration window. Host lineage × virus subtype interactions explained the largest share of variance. Single-agent effects were highly context-dependent; statistically supported antiviral activity was observed only for PCB126 in DF-1 cells infected with H7N3 (q = 0.006). In contrast, a three-compound pollutant mixture significantly enhanced replication in CCL-141 cells infected with H7N3 (q = 3.8 × 10^-4), whereas this supported trend was not observed with FICZ co-exposure. Within the tested environmentally plausible concentration window, concentration-matched Highest Single Agent comparisons more often yielded mixture responses below the strongest matched single-agent response among the evaluated comparisons. Within the tested concentration window, responses were graded and lacked clear thresholds. Overall, AhR-active xenobiotics can tune LPAIV replication in a host- and subtype-specific manner, highlighting the need for mixture-aware, context-dependent ecological infection-risk assessment.
